observation_summary: The compiler crashes with an IllegalStateException when calling getInstanceType() on a FunctionType that does not have an instance type, triggered during the visitNew method in TypeCheck.
reasoning_summary: The fix adds a missing guard condition (fnType.hasInstanceType()) to the existing null check for fnType. This ensures that getInstanceType() is only called when it is safe to do so, preventing the IllegalStateException. This is a classic case of missing validation logic for a method call.
evidence_used: Stack trace shows IllegalStateException at FunctionType.getInstanceType:1071, which is guarded by Preconditions.checkState(hasInstanceType())
The fix diff adds '&& fnType.hasInstanceType()' to the existing 'if (fnType != null)' check in TypeCheck.java

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not a rewrite of the algorithm, but rather the addition of a guard condition to prevent an invalid state from being processed.
The fix does not require a design-level change or a new capability; it simply adds a necessary check to existing code.
